title: Give Your Chat Agent a Voice — Luke Harries, Head of Growth, ElevenLabs

primary.label: Multimodal & Realtime Systems

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk's primary focus is ElevenLabs Voice Engine as a realtime voice/speech system handling STT, TTS, emotion-aware turn-taking, and semantic barge-in for agents. Voice Engine is a general-purpose developer platform that wraps any existing chat agent to add voice, fitting both general-purpose and developer-platforms domains. The talk targets teams with production chat agents and introduces an early-access product seeking design partners. Requires familiarity with chat agent architecture and SDKs but stays at the product and integration level without deep technical depth. Conference presentation featuring a live demo of converting a chat agent to a voice agent in a single prompt. All seven evidence anchors are directly quoted from the transcript with grade said_in_transcript.

summary: Luke Harries frames 2025 as the year of chat agents, noting that products either went AI-first or were left behind. He observes that text-in, text-out already feels dated and argues voice is faster, more accessible, and omni-channel — unlocking phone lines, Zoom calls, screen readers, and ambient interfaces. ElevenLabs initially built text-to-speech models but was pulled into full voice agent solutions while powering customers like Revolut's customer support. The typical architecture combines a voice engine (STT, TTS, turn-taking) with agent orchestration (LLMs, RAG, tool calling, integrations). However, many companies had already built and tuned their chat agents and resisted replacing them entirely. To address this, ElevenLabs previews Voice Engine, a new product that isolates the voice engine layer as a first-class primitive and wraps any existing chat agent via a server SDK. The server SDK creates a client and voice engine, then attaches a wrapper that proxies each new session to the existing chat agent. The client SDK adds a widget in roughly three lines and unlocks telephony and CSaaS out of the box. UI components are based on Shadcn and Vercel styling. A live demo shows converting a generic chat support agent to a voice agent in a single prompt using a bundled skill that analyzes the codebase and generates wrapper code. Harries also mentions a full conversational agents platform for those starting from scratch. He predicts chat agents will either die or add voice, and invites design partners. In Q&A, he explains that tool calling is primarily handled by the existing chat agent backend, though ElevenLabs also supports client-side and server-side tools, with future support for proxying tool calls to the wrapped agent.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and the shift to voice
sections.summary: Harries argues 2025 was the year of chat agents, citing viral examples from Linear, PostHog, and gov.uk. He contends text chat no longer feels like the future and positions voice as a faster, more accessible, omni-channel medium that unlocks phone lines, Zoom calls, and ambient interfaces.

sections.title: Agent architecture and the rebuild problem
sections.summary: ElevenLabs moved from building TTS models to full voice agent solutions, powering customers like Revolut. The typical architecture combines a voice engine with agent orchestration. Many companies had already built chat agents and resisted rebuilding from scratch, motivating a wrapper approach.

sections.title: Introducing Voice Engine
sections.summary: Harries previews Voice Engine, a first-class primitive isolating STT (Scribe), TTS (V3), emotion-context-aware turn-taking, semantic barge-in, and thousands of voices and languages, with a focus on developer experience.

sections.title: Server and client SDKs
sections.summary: The server SDK creates a client and voice engine, then attaches a wrapper that proxies each new session to an existing chat agent. The client SDK adds a widget in roughly three lines and unlocks telephony and CSaaS out of the box. UI components are based on Shadcn and Vercel styling.

sections.title: Demo: converting a chat agent to voice
sections.summary: Harries demonstrates a generic chat support agent and then shows how a bundled skill and a single prompt let a coding agent analyze the codebase and generate the wrapper code to deploy it as a voice agent.

sections.title: Summary and predictions
sections.summary: Two integration paradigms are summarized: Voice Engine for wrapping existing chat agents, and a full conversational agents platform for starting from scratch. Harries predicts chat agents will either die or add voice, and invites design partners.

sections.title: Q&A: Tool calling and integrations
sections.summary: Harries explains that tool calling is primarily handled by the existing chat agent backend, so the wrapper avoids tool-calling complexity. ElevenLabs also supports client-side and server-side tools, with future plans to proxy tool calls to the wrapped agent.
